brief.description: Reference-led continuous cast bed: remove separated feet, integrate control pedestal with solid engine base, extend crankcase toward controller and lower working assembly slightly.
brief.purpose: A grounded late nineteenth-century hot-bulb oil engine: refined fuel and lubricant become visible mechanical work. Compact workshop and future marine equipment.
brief.silhouette: One low stepped cast-iron bed beneath crankcase and long cylinder; open four-spoke flywheel beside it. No separate stands or isolated controller cabinet.
brief.bounds: Existing complete 3x3 slab bed and component anchors unchanged. Continuous cast bed included in controller/cylinder models; same guide air clearances.
brief.materials: Cast iron supports and cabinet sides with restrained material variation; steel caps and actual mounting hardware describe construction. Keep access-cover accents and barrel stripe only where meaningful.
brief.interfaces: Low front-center pedestal, fuel pipe at front and lubricant pipe underneath. Dial and lever remain decorative controls.
brief.states: Stopped/neutral; startup local flame only; working whole wheel turns; shortage/off stops. Preserve casing colors and server-owned state.
brief.construction: Native cuboids and bevels; continuous stepped cast bed split between existing controller and cylinder anchors, perpendicular shaft, enclosed crankcase, single rotating wheel.
brief.invariants: Preserve fuel rates, capacities, recipes and standalone consumer. Construction adds two slabs; ports relocate to front/bottom to keep full base accessible.
fidelity_targets: Continuous cast bed meets cylinder/crankcase and incorporates controller front; no open void above a separate pedestal.
Maintain 24-unit cylinder and 3x3 casing footprint; extend crankcase forward over controls.
Lower shaft/cylinder/wheel together one unit, with verified rotating wheel clearance.
Preserve quiet cast iron, steel collars and small brass fittings; real photo guides structure, not literal dual-wheel replication.
brief.material_behavior: Cast iron with restrained edge wear, machined steel rings, brass only for fittings.
brief.signature_feature: Open flywheel and elongated horizontal cylinder on short grounded iron saddles.

references.role: Identity and functional layout only; refine proportions and native-model detail.
User structural reference: solid grounded bed and compact integrated crankcase; retain single existing wheel and material family.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Create one fresh Minecraft-implementable hot-bulb oil engine mockup for Civilization, set around 1890-1910. One large three-quarter view on a warm light neutral background, no text or alternate designs. Image reference is our refinery texture palette ONLY, not geometry.
A squat 3-block-wide by 3-block-deep steel foundation of half-height slabs. At front center is a low compact instrument/controller pedestal, leaving both front corners clear for pipe connections. Behind it, a horizontal medium-gray cast-iron engine cylinder and supported crankcase occupy the middle, with a large exposed four-spoke octagonal flywheel on the LEFT. Copper utility block at rear, short plain exhaust. All machinery stands on substantial feet meeting the half-height bed. Cylinder points fore-aft; flywheel axle runs left-right, physically into a bearing and closed crankcase. Keep connecting rod enclosed inside that crankcase, eliminating exposed linkage crossing the wheel. Wheel is a single coherent rotating unit with four thick spokes and clear empty openings; its bottom clears the foundation. Mechanically plausible and solid, not ornate.
Render as an actual Blockbench Minecraft asset: only cuboids and limited 45-degree bevels, deliberately chunky 32-texel-per-block pixel textures, no tiny geometric bolts, no smooth high-poly curves. Medium graphite iron, muted blue-gray steel, restrained warm brass fittings and one small cream-faced instrument. Match reference material tone but use clean readable planes and subtle wear, not noisy texture. Rivets and panel lines painted into textures. Soft neutral daylight, honest shadows, no bloom, no cinematic smoke, no schematic floating parts. The assembly must look buildable from a handful of Minecraft pieces, handsome yet simple.

Edit this exact engine mockup, preserving its handsome cast-iron/steel/brass palette, chunky Minecraft cuboid style, large four-spoke octagonal left flywheel, low front-center dial controller, lighting and camera. Fix three construction issues. 1: The engine cylinder must run FRONT TO BACK, perpendicular to the flywheel axle which runs LEFT TO RIGHT. Put a compact CLOSED rectangular crankcase beside the flywheel hub, then the cylinder extending rearward from that crankcase. The cylinder axis must be perpendicular to the flywheel shaft, not an extension of it. No exposed connecting rod. 2: Remove the front-left and front-right foundation blocks, leaving a T-shaped footprint: two full rows of three half-height foundation slabs behind the lone front-center controller. Leave both controller sides accessible to pipes. The wheel is supported at its HUB by bearing pedestals, its rim clears the bed completely, no foot touching rim. 3: Remove the big elevated copper tank; replace with a low copper slab at the BACK under utility fittings. Keep one modest plain exhaust and a small brass oiler on the cylinder, no extra machinery. One view, no labels. This is a targeted correction, not a new art direction.

Edit ONLY the flywheel supports in this exact Minecraft engine mockup. Preserve every other part, geometry, camera, colors and textures. Remove both little feet that touch the bottom edge of the flywheel. The flywheel RIM must float free around its AXLE with a clearly visible empty gap underneath, at least the thickness of its rim. Add ONE strong vertical bearing pedestal BEHIND the wheel, extending from foundation up to the AXLE HUB height, hidden partly by the spokes. This stationary pedestal must sit behind the plane of the rotating wheel and support its axle, never touch the rim. Wheel stays same size and height. No other edits. Maintain open gaps between spokes so bearing and shaft can be understood.

Simplify this exact engine drawing. REMOVE THE ENTIRE PEDESTAL UNDER AND BEHIND THE LEFT FLYWHEEL, including its brass base and foot. The wheel must be supported ONLY by its SHORT HORIZONTAL AXLE going from the wheel center INTO the adjacent large gray crankcase on the RIGHT. The existing crankcase has its own strong foundation foot and acts as the bearing. Leave a large unmistakably EMPTY AIR GAP beneath the entire rotating wheel: no supports under the wheel at all. Keep the wheel, hub, axle, crankcase, cylinder, controller, bed and every other part exactly unchanged. Do not add other parts. This is a physically credible overhung flywheel with its bearing inside the crankcase, not a rim sitting on a stand. Same Minecraft pixel-textured style and camera.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the referenced selected Minecraft hot-bulb oil engine mockup, preserving its coherent Tesla-era style and all attractive structural detail. One design, one large three-quarter product view on neutral warm beige. Remove the copper strip/panel behind the cylinder entirely: no copper slab or copper structural plate anywhere. Use two short broad integrated cast-iron feet with restrained brass ankle bands supporting the crankcase and rear cylinder. Preserve the octagonal four-spoke flywheel, enclosed compact beveled crankcase, horizontal faceted cylindrical barrel with two raised end flanges, separate hot bulb, small brass oil cup, short exhaust with collar, low steel T-shaped bed and small front-center analog control pedestal. Barrel length should be about 1.5 times its diameter and its horizontal form must be obvious. Shaft must enter side of crankcase and be perpendicular to barrel axis. No moving part intersects a foot. Keep details achievable with Minecraft Java cuboids and 45 degree bevels, textures for rivets and seams, simple meaningful small fittings, no realistic thin tubing or smooth high-poly curves. Medium blue-gray cast iron with muted steel edge bands, small warm brass accents, crisp painted pixel-art materials. Preserve the reference's layered craftsmanship, readable mechanical mass and proportions; do not simplify it into tall rectangular boxes. No labels or text.

Use case: stylized-concept. Create one refined Minecraft/Blockbench-implementable hot-bulb oil engine concept, not competing designs. Reference image 1 supplies identity/layout, image 2 supplies restrained iron/steel/enamel material family only. Render one complete engine in clear rear three-quarter view, wheel on left and cylinder extending right. Quiet warm gray background, no text.
Preserve the perpendicular crankshaft and horizontal cylinder axes, four open spokes and octagonal flywheel, elongated cylinder with end flanges, short substantial iron supports, low bed of steel half slabs and small front control cabinet. Improve craftsmanship: a thinner layered wheel rim with machined outer band and deep open quadrants, substantial central hub, a stepped crankcase with readable access hatch, discrete fasteners, two narrower cylinder flanges, a small brass hot bulb and burner, small top oil cup, short hollow exhaust stack. Raised brass-rimmed cream dial and physical lever on control cabinet. No giant copper slab. No decorative gears. Do not add pipes that cross the wheel sweep.
Geometry must look like an ACTUAL native Minecraft cuboid model using axis-aligned cubes and modest 45-degree bevels, no smooth meshes, no tiny machined ridges, no fantasy curves. Clean broad surfaces, restrained pixel clusters, roughly 32 texels per block. Gray-blue cast iron body, slightly lighter steel edge strips, warm brass only fittings. No excessive brass, no black unreadable mechanism, no baked dramatic glow. Carefully supported feet contact the bed, wheel clears bed and body at every angle. Target readable large shapes and secondary fittings rather than illustration detail. Keep silhouette close to the reference but make it refined and functional.

Use case: stylized-concept. Texture master for Civilization's Tesla-era cast iron oil engine. Reference 1 defines cast iron, steel and brass palette. Reference 2 is the native engine model to understand parts only. Create ONE flat orthographic high-resolution pixel-art texture sheet, four equal square quadrants, no gutters no text labels. Top left: a dark iron ACCESS PANEL with a narrow recessed seam inside perimeter, short silver worn L-shaped corner brackets, small steel corner rivets, a restrained thin warm brass double-line inlay on the inner border, quieter textured iron center. Top right: a STEEL EDGE TRIM panel, broad silver steel face with dark perimeter seam, narrow polished outer edge and four darker fasteners; controlled longitudinal machining strokes, no noisy scratches. Bottom left: dark cast iron BODY PANEL, broad dark iron field with thin stepped steel edges and sparse clustered wear at corners; inset muted blue-green enamel narrow horizontal stripe across middle, not glowing, no symbols. Bottom right: a dark iron FOOT/SUPPORT PANEL with inset rectangular cast recess, subtle vertical casting ribs near left/right sides, steel corner accents, one small plain aged brass identification plate centered near top, no lettering. Keep each panel aligned to its square boundaries and all patterns large enough for a native game texture. Strong deliberate pixel clusters and readable corner treatment. High-resolution pixel-art master, no tiny output request, no subpixel scratches, no gradients, no photorealism. Fully opaque edge-to-edge. These panels should look crafted and maintained, not ruined, not ornate steampunk. Preserve dark iron body with restrained steel/brass accents.

Refine this exact Minecraft Blockbench oil engine design, not a new design. Preserve cast iron, steel corner accents, brass fittings, teal stripe, octagonal four-spoke flywheel and readable low control box. Make the bed a complete square 3 by 3 grid of half-height steel casing blocks (front-center occupied by the control pedestal), no missing front corners. Engine should read longer and less stubby: move crankcase and flywheel forward and extend the straight horizontal cylinder by one third, keeping the heated brass bulb at the back end and two grounded feet. Maintain a clear gap between wheel and bed throughout rotation. Support posts should end at the underside of their steel top plates with no overlapping exposed faces. Everything economical Minecraft cuboids and 45-degree bevels, native-looking pixel materials. Three-quarter rear view like the reference on a neutral background. No labels, no extra machinery, no copper slab.

Correct this exact Minecraft engine reference: REMOVE the disconnected third support pedestal in the foreground middle of the base. Edit this exact Minecraft engine image only by simplifying the two cast-iron support feet and control box side surfaces. Redesign this Minecraft hot-bulb engine using the real engine photo as structural reference. One continuous low stepped CAST IRON BED under the crankcase and long cylinder, not two separate support stands.
